analysis:
The PR changes only docs/reference/configuration.md. The head ranges 586-595 add a 'Prompt preparation and admission' section for DARKBLOOM_TTFT_PROMPT_CACHE, _MB, _VERIFY, TTFT_TEMPLATE_LOOPS and TTFT_COLD_LOAD_RELEASE. The supplied units are base text only (lines 1-518), so the added lines and the truncated patch excerpt were not fully visible. No code or control change is observable. The documented behavior still carries security-relevant design questions for the code review pass.

1. T-041 / A-001: a per-scope prompt-token piece cache is described as keyed to the request's prefix-cache scope (the coordinator-authored cacheSalt). If the implementation is not scope-isolated, it could add a cross-tenant timing or sharing channel beyond the accepted SEC-035 in-process TTFT oracle. This cannot be verified from the docs alone. The doc says the global DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE disable also turns it off, which is consistent with T-041's kill switch.

2. Memory residency: the cache holds pieces of decrypted prompt text or tokens in process memory. Capacity is up to 4096 MiB, default 32 MiB. This is in-process only and falls under the existing T-011/T-014/T-028 posture. It is unclear whether any of it is persisted, and the doc does not claim so.

3. Integrity: the background verification, with a mismatch disabling reuse, is a mitigation. The default interval is 256, with the first 4 prompts checked.

Other base text, such as the Local GLM qualification and App Attest worker sections, is unchanged context and consistent with TB-011 and T-053. No finding is reported. A deeper review of PromptTokenCache.swift scope keying and eviction is recommended if that file is in another batch.
